svg.aria-label: Queen and Kafka at 3 million messages a second from 10 to 10 million partitions: end to end latency, broker CPU, memory and disk writes
svg.text: Queen 2.4 and Kafka 4.3.1 at 3M msg/s, one queue or topic, 10 to 10M partitions
Three GCP c4-standard-24-lssd brokers (24 vCPU, 88 GB, four NVMe disks in RAID0) and three 16-vCPU loaders · Kafka 10-14, Queen 10-15

partitions in one queue or topic (each step is 10 times the one before)

svg.text: CPU, cores of the three brokers (of 72)
Memory of the busiest broker, GB (of 88)
Fresh cluster a point, 70 s of load, 100 messages of 256 B a request, nine load processes, the same settings as the DigitalOcean comparison of 2026-10-13.
Kafka: three replicas, acks=all, min.insync 2, idempotent producer, lz4, linger 5 ms, 6 GB heap; writes go to the page cache (no fsync per write);
XFS noatime, 24 request handler, 12 network and 12 replica fetcher threads, writeback from 1 GB of dirty pages (on ext4 its p99 was up to ten times higher).
Kafka between the drawn counts: 25k partitions carried, p50 / p99 58 / 105 ms on 57 cores; 50k not carried (601k msg/s pushed); Queen not run there.
Queen 2.4: 2.3.0 plus three changes that cut the bytes written a message, not released; XFS noatime; binary push, zstd, counted acks.
A Queen write is answered after the leader's fsync and one follower's; framed pops; dedup off; 10M with QUEEN_CONSUME_IDLE_UNLOAD_S=30.
Queen at 1,000 partitions: the median of five runs (their p99: 15, 17, 18, 20, 65 ms). Kafka's memory leaves out the page cache it reads from.
